description: The road safety open data are record-level files of personal injury road collisions in Great Britain reported to the police and recorded with the STATS19 system, with separate tables for collisions (date, time, location, road class and number, junction, speed limit, light, weather and surface conditions, severity), vehicles involved and casualties. They are published by the Department for Transport. Coverage is Great Britain from 1979 to the latest final year (2025), located by coordinates, with provisional January to June data each November. Files are coded CSV with a data guide for decoding: yearly files of 10 to 21 MB, the last five years, and the complete 1979 to latest series of about 1 to 2 GB per table, free under the Open Government Licence; sensitive fields such as contributory factors are available on request. Caveats: only injury collisions reported to police are included, the move to injury-based severity reporting by some forces requires the provided severity adjustments, and coding changes (for example e-scooters from September 2026) are logged in revision notes. The data support hazard exposure, emergency response and road safety policy studies, calibration of traffic safety models, and resilience analysis of road networks; the independent stats19 R package, built on these files, offers programmatic access.
